root_cause.text: The libata drive-quirks table did not mark the Seagate ST1000DM010-2EP102 as `ATA_QUIRK_NOLPM`, so `libata-core` allowed link power management on a disk family known to misbehave under LPM and freeze the system.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `{"ST1000DM010-2EP102", NULL, ATA_QUIRK_NOLPM}` under “Seagate disks with LPM issues” in `drivers/ata/libata-core.c`, and the commit message says this model has “problems with LPM, causing random system freezes.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a no-LPM quirk for the Seagate ST1000DM010-2EP102 to work around its LPM issues.
intent_record.what: A new ATA device quirk entry was added for the Seagate model "ST1000DM010-2EP102", assigning it the ATA_QUIRK_NOLPM flag alongside an existing list of Seagate disks with LPM issues.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes the ATA layer to disable Link Power Management for that specific drive model, avoiding the LPM-related problems the drive exhibits.

candidates.rationale: This is the existing Seagate drive-quirks entry for LPM problems. The vulnerability stems from the absence of a corresponding ATA_QUIRK_NOLPM entry for ST1000DM010-2EP102 in this same table section, allowing LPM on a known-bad drive family.
This comment identifies the exact quirk group implicated by the root cause. The vulnerable condition is that the affected Seagate model was missing from this LPM-issues section.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix table entry shows the Seagate LPM-quirk section where the missing ST1000DM010-2EP102 no-LPM entry should have been added. The vulnerability is the absence of the corresponding ATA_QUIRK_NOLPM quirk for the affected drive family, which allowed libata to enable LPM on a model known to misbehave and freeze.
